description: Crypto Village focuses on cryptographic protocols, privacy preservation, secure communications, data protection, and surveillance defense.

talks.title: What If We Had TLS for Phone Numbers?
talks.teaser: Explores applying TLS-style cryptographic identity and encryption primitives to telephone networks to mitigate spoofing and call interception.

talks.title: Fear Uncertainty and Doubt

talks.title: Online Voting
talks.teaser: Analyzes the cryptographic and privacy challenges of implementing secure end-to-end verifiable online voting systems.

talks.title: Hacking Like Paris Hilton
talks.teaser: Reflects on the infamous Paris Hilton Sidekick hack, analyzing account takeover tactics, security questions, and modern authentication flaws.

talks.title: How to Store Sensitive Info in 2020?
talks.teaser: Reviews best practices and modern architectural patterns for encrypting and securely storing sensitive data in cloud environments.

talks.title: Fun with FOIA

talks.title: Crypto and Privacy Fireside Chat
talks.teaser: A fireside chat discussing ongoing encryption battles, government backdoor legislation, and digital civil liberties.

talks.title: STARTTLS is Dangerous
talks.teaser: Hanno Böck reveals critical flaws in STARTTLS implementations across mail servers and clients, demonstrating command injection and credential theft via protocol downgrade attacks.
talks.summary:
The Inherent Fragility of STARTTLS

The STARTTLS mechanism was designed to opportunistically upgrade plaintext application protocols (such as SMTP, IMAP, and POP3) to encrypted TLS sessions, but its design introduces severe architectural risks.

Command Injection in Mail Transfer Agents

Hanno Böck revisits classic protocol flaws—including Wietse Venema's 2011 Postfix vulnerability—showing that command injection across plaintext-to-ciphertext transitions remains pervasive in modern mail servers.

Client-Side Credential Theft

Böck reveals that widespread email clients are equally susceptible to machine-in-the-middle command injection, allowing attackers to hijack authentication sessions and harvest plaintext user credentials.

Abandoning Opportunistic Upgrades

The speaker demonstrates ambiguous and contradictory RFC specifications governing STARTTLS, arguing that the security community must deprecate STARTTLS in favor of strict implicit TLS connections.
